analysis:
RECOMMENDATION
Implement a native, coordinator-managed review skill plus a small Node artifact validator. Support the native collaboration host available in this session, with explicitly limited lifecycle guarantees. Do not retain the external #9 runner in the initial replacement. Keep review orchestration and result schemas independent of cross-design. Extract only the mechanical artifact functions actually used by both workflows.

EVIDENCE AND LIMITS
Verified by read-only inspection: skills/cross-design/scripts/protocol.mjs owns snapshot hashes, exclusive file creation, unique attempts, request/response hashes, deadline admission, retry accounting and design-specific phase transitions. Its record() does not validate transport receipts. Its references/transports.md expressly assigns lifecycle observation to the coordinator, rejects plausible output after transport failure, and distinguishes managed-turn interruption from remote shutdown. README.md documents whole-plugin installation and per-skill scripts, with Node 20.11+ and node --test skills/*/scripts/*.test.mjs. These observations agree with inputs/brief.md. I did not inspect other proposals, run code, validate the current Git revision or independently reproduce #9 failures. The failures and #13 qualification limits are supplied evidence, not new verification. The architecture below is a recommendation, not a claim that all host behaviors have already been qualified.

MODEL AND TRANSPORT POLICY
Use two fresh contexts with explicitly configured distinct model bindings: gpt-6.1-sol and gpt-6-astra in this environment, subject to repository/user selections. Same-provider operation is supported; cross-provider operation is neither required nor advertised. Record requested binding, configured binding and independently observed identity separately; unknown resolved identity remains unknown. Never substitute silently or count two instances of the same binding as two distinct models. Unavailable required bindings produce an incomplete review with any usable partial findings retained.

The coordinator launches through spawn_agent with fresh context and the saved request, captures the returned handle, collects the final response through native final notifications, observes lifecycle with list_agents and requests interruption through interrupt_agent. These are the actual available controls, not a proposed bridge. A final response is necessary but does not alone prove that the run met its deadline or that cancellation is effective. Save the original final response and a coordinator-owned receipt with attempt ID, handle, configured binding, dispatch observation, terminal outcome, observation times and cancellation scope. The receipt schema belongs to cross-review; it is evidence supplied by the coordinator, not cryptographic attestation from the host.

Before dispatch, recheck both run and attempt deadlines. While a call is active, keep coordinator waits short enough to check deadlines, at most 30 seconds. At deadline, request interruption and observe the managed turn becoming terminal. No accepted late response, and no retry while termination is unknown. This supports managed deadlines while the coordinator is operating, not automatic unattended wall-clock termination. If the coordinator is interrupted, outstanding attempts become unaccepted/unknown; on recovery, reconcile handles and cancel remaining work before proceeding. Expired runs cannot resume discovery or accept responses. Cleanup may outlast the budget and must be reported separately. If boundedness is intended to require autonomous termination even after coordinator loss, this native path is insufficient and implementation must stop advertising that stronger guarantee.

ARTIFACT AND CODE BOUNDARY
Add proposed skills/cross-review/SKILL.md, discovery.md, challenge.md, verification.md, scripts/protocol.mjs and tests, with references describing the result schema and host procedure. Proposed paths are design choices, not existing files. Extract a small proposed lib/artifacts.mjs containing deterministic file-tree hashing and symlink rejection, immutable snapshot copy, exclusive writes, unique attempt allocation, digest/identity verification and explicit-time deadline predicates. Both skill-local protocol modules import it. Do not extract phases, statuses, retry policy, prompt composition, adjudication, transport supervision or model routing. Preserve cross-design's public init/prepare/record/fail interface and semantics; migrate its mechanical operations with its existing tests unchanged.

A root lib dependency is acceptable only after demonstrating that the actual supported plugin archive includes it and skill-directory symlinks resolve imports to the checkout. Test each helper from a copied plugin tree without access to the source checkout and through real symlinks. Do not advertise standalone copying of an individual skill directory. If the plugin packager excludes lib, change the packaging or the dependency location before shipment; do not rely on an undocumented sibling lookup or add a general loader.

SNAPSHOT AND SCOPE
Preparation resolves the repository identity and both requested revision selectors to full base/head commits; records selector names as well as resolved commits; generates the diff itself from those pinned commits with a fixed, recorded Git argument vector; and hashes its exact bytes. Disable external diff/text conversion and document whether the comparison is direct base-to-head or merge-base-to-head. Default to direct pinned base-to-head; if a PR requires a merge base, resolve and record that commit explicitly. Supplied free-form diff text is contextual evidence, never the authoritative reviewed change.

Snapshot the scoped contract, relevant evidence, reviewer prompts, bindings, diff metadata and diff bytes once. Keep these shared inputs unchanged throughout the run. Reviewer source inspection must refer to pinned commits or prepared source views rather than a mutable working tree. Initially support committed reviews and reject ambiguity about uncommitted work. At closeout, re-resolve both original selectors and compare both pins, regenerate the diff with the same recipe, and revalidate snapshot hashes. A moved base matters just as much as a moved head. Findings remain historical evidence when pins move, but the report is stale and cannot claim currency.

The scoped contract explicitly lists this PR's obligations, contextual links, downstream exclusions and any justified evidence fetched from a contextual source. Referenced issues do not recursively expand obligations. Release and Kavtsya migration remain excluded under #8.

Each attempt has an exclusive fresh directory and immutable request. Retries reference the same snapshot and get a new attempt ID and output paths. Never clean earlier attempt directories during a live run. Acceptance verifies snapshot, request and attempt identity, deadline, schema, successful terminal receipt and absence of prior failed/cancelled disposition. Store accepted response bytes and their digest. Failed or cancelled output is retained only as diagnostic data. Raw output from another attempt cannot satisfy an acceptance path.

REVIEW OWNERSHIP AND RESULTS
Both reviewers independently assess correctness, failure behavior and affected invariants against the scoped contract; assign one primary ownership of behavior/regressions and the other primary ownership of failure paths/invariants, without forbidding overlap. Repository standards and maintainability advice remain additional evidence, not an automatic blocking category. Prompts require inspected coverage, reasoning, limitations and structured findings.

An expert response has completion COMPLETE or INCOMPLETE, nonempty analysis, a nonempty coverage description, limitations and findings. A COMPLETE response may have findings: []. INCOMPLETE must include specific missing work. Findings carry an attempt-local stable ID, location, claim, supporting evidence, confidence, impact and proposed disposition. The coordinator assigns stable run-level IDs and retains mappings when deduplicating. Use separate confidence values such as confirmed/supported/uncertain, impact such as behavioral/advisory, and disposition such as blocking/advisory/rejected/unresolved/fixed. A confirmed cosmetic problem is advisory. A change-caused regression outside changed lines may block. INCOMPLETE is a structured field, never a prose marker parsed by blank-line heuristics. Nonempty text is necessary for structural acceptance but cannot mechanically prove substantive review; the coordinator must check whether claimed coverage and evidence are meaningful.

Adjudication records each claim's evidence, causal relationship to the change, decision and reason. Compare against the base when necessary to distinguish regression from existing behavior. Confirmation requires source reasoning or a focused observation, never agreement alone. Retain rejected claims and dissent, especially when the coordinator authored the change. Challenge only consequential unresolved claims, supplying their exact IDs, adjudication revision hash and discriminating evidence. Settled findings reopen only for new evidence.

Use separate final dimensions: execution usable/incomplete; review complete/incomplete; currency current/stale/unknown; finding disposition blocking/unresolved/advisory/none; and readiness evidence. A completed review with blocking findings is a completed review, not a runtime failure. A clean completed review means no supported blocking finding was established within recorded coverage; it is not proof of completeness or general readiness. Readiness depends on the required checks actually performed and current pins. Unresolved potentially blocking claims remain explicit uncertainty.

BUDGETS AND OPTIONAL REPAIR
Default review-only budget: 30 minutes total, 10 minutes per call, two discovery calls, at most two targeted challenge calls in one cycle, and one transient retry per expert across all phases. Thus at most six calls, with the total clock taking precedence. Retries require observed terminal failure and a reason classified as transient; malformed findings or disagreement do not automatically justify retry. Additional discovery is excluded by default.

When repair mode is selected at initialization, permit one repair batch and at most two focused verification calls within the same total clock: at most eight calls including the two possible retries. Repair does not imply commit, push, merge or risk acceptance. Each repaired revision gets a new immutable snapshot linked to the prior snapshot and finding IDs; never mutate the initial snapshot. Verification covers the previous finding, changed code and affected behavior, using executable checks where useful. If repair creates a concrete new risk requiring broad discovery, record the reason and request a separately budgeted continuation rather than silently restarting convergence. Budget exhaustion produces partial evidence and unresolved findings. Advisory-only findings permit normal stopping.

STRONGEST ALTERNATIVE
Retain and repair the external #9 process supervisor, plus the same new review artifact and adjudication protocol. Its advantage is independently testable process deadlines and local descendant cleanup even while a model coordinator is idle. Its costs are maintaining subprocess/provider configuration, qualifying the exact CLI interfaces, preserving supervisor tests and solving more operational problems than this session requires. It also does not automatically prove remote-provider shutdown. Choose it instead only if unattended hard deadlines, an unavailable native model binding or a required external provider is an actual requirement. The cheapest deciding observation is a concrete statement of whether coordinator-loss termination is required; then a bounded installed-host lifecycle probe, not another architecture debate.

IMPLEMENTATION AND VERIFICATION
First record the exact candidate, challenge results, decisions and dissent. Next add regression fixtures for the demonstrated failures and implement the review-specific schema/acceptance gate. Then extract only the proven common primitives while preserving cross-design interfaces and tests. Add coordinator instructions, receipt validation, bounded budgets, adjudication and repair snapshot linkage. Finally verify packaging, documentation and live behavior.

Automated observable cases: blank/empty/malformed response rejected; structured INCOMPLETE retained as incomplete regardless of whitespace; completed empty findings accepted with substantive required fields; interrupted attempt's report cannot satisfy a retry; retry creation leaves peer-readable inputs intact; wrong IDs/hashes and modified snapshots rejected; moved base or head makes closeout stale; generated diff differs from pins and is rejected; failed/cancelled/unknown transport with plausible JSON cannot be accepted; late reservation, dispatch admission and acceptance fail; unknown cancellation prevents retry; advisory-only outcomes stop; accepted blocking claims can cite unchanged lines; repair creates a distinct snapshot. Use a fake clock and recorded transport observations to test artifact decisions, while explicitly labeling them insufficient to qualify native cancellation.

Run bounded live cases for a known defect, a clean change and a disputed/advisory claim, plus authorized repair with focused verification. Record found and missed issues, rejected claims, actual calls, elapsed time, budget omissions and lifecycle receipts. Separately probe native interruption and coordinator recovery with harmless work before advertising those supported behaviors. Preserve cross-design tests and run the README's documented Node test command plus the repository's actual plugin checks after inspecting them. Replacement PR documentation explains #9 supersession and remaining limits; publication and migration stay in #8.
concerns: The available native controls do not establish automatic termination after coordinator interruption. Confirm that supported boundedness means admission/acceptance limits plus active coordinator-managed interruption; otherwise qualify a real supervisor before claiming compliance.

The native tool's precise observable distinction between successful final completion, failed completion and interrupted idle state needs a bounded lifecycle probe. Until demonstrated, unknown outcomes must stay unaccepted and must not unlock retry.

Root lib packaging and symlink import behavior must be demonstrated with the actual plugin artifact and supported linked installation; README documents layouts but does not establish this proposed shared dependency.

The brief does not define how callers specify mutable base/head selectors or uncommitted reviews. The smallest initial contract is committed revisions with both original selectors recorded and rechecked; supporting working-tree changes would require an explicit additional snapshot contract.
